subject: Packaging options and safe upgrade path for Brightline
messages:
From: Alice Tully <alice.tully@brightline.health>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@brightline.health
Date: 2026-07-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Packaging options and upgrade/downgrade clarity

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency numbers and the Dedicated options. Before we get procurement involved, we need a clear description of packaging choices and the implications for upgrading/downgrading mid-contract. Two specific asks: a) what happens if our monthly throughput spikes 3x for a quarter (upgrade path + credits), and b) how feature bundling works — can we enable certain enterprise features (KV cache retention and per-route tracing) only for specific routes without moving the whole account to a higher tier?

Also, procurement asked for a simple spreadsheet of pricing scenarios (steady, spike, canary pilot) you can share. Can you send that and a recommended rollback guardrail?

Appreciate it — Alice
Alice Tully
Head of Platform Integrations
Brightline Health

Attachments: none

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Tully <alice.tully@brightline.health>
Cc: procurement@brightline.health
Date: 2026-07-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options and upgrade/downgrade clarity

Hi Alice — great meeting, thanks for the clear asks.

Short answers up front:
- Spikes: we support quick (minutes) burst capacity for short spikes and a stepwise upgrade for sustained increases. For a 3x sustained quarterly spike we recommend a temporary Dedicated burst plus a 3-month committed uplift with a retroactive credit to smooth billing — see the attached pricing_scenarios.xlsx for numbers.
- Feature-level enablement: yes, you can enable platform features per-route via our routing policy and entitlements; that lets you keep most traffic on the core tier while routing critical routes to an enterprise bundle that includes KV retention and tracing. That approach avoids a full-account tier jump.
- Rollback/canary: recommend a canary with 5% traffic for 48 hours, auto-fallback to core model variant, and a quota-based hard stop if error rate > 2% for 15 minutes.

I've attached: Brightline_MAAP_v2.pdf (proposed minimal-assured-availability plan) and pricing_scenarios.xlsx (steady/spike/canary scenarios). Let me know if you want a single-line commercial offer we can hand to procurement. Happy to hop on a call Friday.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Brightline_MAAP_v2.pdf; pricing_scenarios.xlsx
Related: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cBrightlineDocs

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-31T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Packaging options and upgrade/downgrade clarity — pricing ask (Brightline)

Ben / Lauren — forwarding Alice's note and my quick responses. Procurement wants a clean spreadsheet and a single-line commercial option they can slot into an internal PO. Key decision points:
- We can offer a 3-month uplift commit with a 10% credit for unused burst (to reduce sticker shock); is 10% the right anchor or do we lean 15% for strategic accounts?
- Feature gating per-route needs to be operationally simple; Lauren, can we confirm console toggles + API entitlements are accessible to their SREs without additional seat/licenses?

Proposed approach: present three scenarios in the sheet (steady, spike-commit, pilot canary). For commercial, include a 6% early-commit discount if they sign a 9-month amendment to the current quote.

Thoughts?

— Mateo

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-31T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Packaging options and upgrade/downgrade clarity — pricing ask (Brightline)

Mateo — good framing. A couple of practical points:
- 10% unused-burst credit seems conservative; for a strategic pilot I'd back 12.5% (keeps it simple but shows concession).
- The early-commit 6% is fine, but make sure the math on effective unit price at 3x usage is explicit (procurement will run it through their internal model).
- On feature gating, confirm with Product that enabling per-route tracing does not require a higher entitlement SKU beyond the toggles (we can't force them to buy seats just to turn on tracing). If Product pushes a SKU, we need to surface that early.

If you want, I can join the call Friday and help walk through the numbers.

— Ben
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Alice Tully <alice.tully@brightline.health>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@brightline.health
Date: 2026-08-01T10:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options and upgrade/downgrade clarity

Thanks Mateo — the attachments look useful. A few clarifying questions before procurement schedules a review:

1) Canary to production: can we do a progressive canary (5% -> 20% -> 60%) with automated rollback rules and manual approve for the 60% step? We want an ops-friendly rollback flow.
2) Billing and credits: for the 3-month uplift, is the credit applied monthly or as an end-of-term reconciliation? Procurement prefers monthly bill smoothing.
3) Entitlements visibility: procurement asked whether per-route features show up as separate line items on the bill or are absorbed under a single SKU.

If you can confirm those three points, procurement will prepare an internal memo. Also — can you provide a one-pager that maps packaging choices to typical SRE runbooks (upgrade checklist, rollback commands, monitoring thresholds)?

Best,
Alice

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>

Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, procurement@brightline.health
Date: 2026-08-02T15:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options and upgrade/downgrade clarity — next steps

Alice — answering your three bullets and next steps below: 

1) Progressive canary: supported. We recommend 5% -> 20% (24 hours each) -> 60% (manual approve). Canary automations include an instantaneous fallback switch and an automated rollback if aggregated error or latency breach thresholds are hit (we'll provide the playbook).

2) Credits: we can apply the unused-burst credit monthly to smooth billing. We'll show both monthly and EOT reconciliation numbers in the commercial. For Brightline I implemented the 12.5% unused-burst credit as Ben suggested — it shows well vs. their internal model.

3) Entitlements on bill: per-route entitlements appear as line items tied to the route ID (they are grouped under a single SKU on the invoice but include route-level metadata for visibility). Procurement will see a single SKU with metadata tags for each enabled route.

Attached: updated pricing_scenarios.xlsx (with monthly-credit rows) and Brightline_MAAP_v2.pdf. Also adding a one-page ops playbook to the Drive (link below). For procurement, I've prepared a single-line commercial we can move to DocuSign once you confirm the uplift length (3 months vs 6 months).

Next steps:
- If Brightline confirms 3-month uplift with 12.5% monthly unused-burst credit, I'll generate the amendment and send the DocuSign.
- Schedule a 30-min call Thursday to walk procurement through the invoice view and canary steps.

DocuSign preview: https://redwood.ai/docusign/preview/DL-2026-0847
